memories.author: D04
memories.text:
- Chronic urticaria
  - Status: Persistent daily wheals, mild pruritus, no angioedema. Weight 62 kg, waist 84 cm (female cutoff 80 cm, increased).
  - Plan: Continue levocetirizine 5 mg OD after food. Add cetirizine 10 mg HS if breakthrough. Review symptom diary.
- Migraine
  - Status: 2–3 episodes/month, responsive to sumatriptan. No new neurological signs.
  - Plan: Start propranolol 40 mg OD after food for prophylaxis. Continue sumatriptan 50 mg SOS after food. Topiramate 25 mg HS after food, naproxen 500 mg SOS after food as needed.
- General health
  - Status: Otherwise well, drives locally. No fever.
  - Plan: Annual lipid profile due. Weight and waist monitored each visit.
Due: HbA1c in 3 months (routine).

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
Neurological examination: Normal cranial nerves, no focal deficits, normal gait.
CT head (plain): No acute hemorrhage, infarct, or mass lesion. Chronic microvascular changes age-appropriate.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
Referral to Dr. S. Rao, Neurology, Vikram Hospital.
Reason: Evaluation of migraine prophylaxis and exclude secondary headache.
Clinical details: 90‑year‑old female driver, migraine 1‑2/month on propranolol, normal neuro exam and CT head. Request opinion on continuing prophylaxis and possible CGRP inhibitor.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
Letter from Dr. S. Rao (Neurology):
Migraine appears typical, prophylaxis with propranolol adequate. No indication for CGRP inhibitor given age and limited benefit. Continue current regimen, ensure BP monitoring. Return to primary care for routine follow‑up.
